```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Miura et al. (2026) fitted four independent one-compartment population PK
models with first-order absorption to routine clinical plasma concentrations
from Japanese paediatric (< 15 years) and adult (>= 15 years) patients with
pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH): two phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors
(sildenafil, tadalafil) and two endothelin receptor antagonists (bosentan,
ambrisentan). Each drug is packaged as its own model.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Miura_2026_sildenafil"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70676>

```{r load-models}
drugs <- c("sildenafil", "tadalafil", "bosentan", "ambrisentan")
mods <- setNames(
  lapply(paste0("Miura_2026_", drugs), function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n))),
  drugs
)
for (d in drugs) {
  cat(sprintf("Miura_2026_%s: %s\n\n", d, mods[[d]]$description))
}
```

# Population

The analysis pooled 35 paediatric and 16 adult Japanese patients with PAH
treated at Hamamatsu University Hospital and Seirei Hamamatsu Hospital. Each
drug's model was fitted to the patients receiving it (Table 1): sildenafil 24
patients (15 paediatric / 9 adult, 297 concentrations), tadalafil 31 (20 / 11,
157), bosentan 16 (7 / 9, 189) and ambrisentan 29 (18 / 11, 177). Paediatric
median ages were 1.8-5.0 years (range 0.1-14.8) and median body weights
10.1-16.5 kg; adult median weights were 48.5-52.3 kg. Most patients were female
(61-69%). Concentrations came from routine clinical sampling, some of it from
two earlier steady-state studies, and were measured in patients on
monotherapy or on combinations of a PDE-5 inhibitor and an endothelin receptor
antagonist.

```{r population}
pop_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(drugs, function(d) {
  p <- mods[[d]]$population
  tibble(
    Drug = d,
    N = p$n_subjects,
    Concentrations = p$n_observations,
    `Age (years)` = p$age_range,
    `Weight median (kg)` = p$weight_median,
    `Female (%)` = p$sex_female_pct
  )
}))
knitr::kable(pop_tbl)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them. All structural and covariate values are from Table 2
(sildenafil, tadalafil) and Table 3 (bosentan, ambrisentan); the covariate
equations are the footnotes of those tables.

| Drug | Parameter | Value | Source |
|------|-----------|-------|--------|
| sildenafil | `lka` | log(4.51), not estimated | Table 2 (literature value, ref 25) |
| sildenafil | `lcl` | log(60.6) L/h | Table 2 |
| sildenafil | `lvc` | log(322) L | Table 2 |
| sildenafil | `e_wt_cl` | 0.537 | Table 2, Effect of BW |
| sildenafil | `e_conmed_bosentan_cl` | 0.633 | Table 2, Effect of BOS |
| sildenafil | `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.563^2, 0.255^2 | Table 2, IIV 56.3%, 25.5% |
| sildenafil | `propSd` | 0.585 | Table 2, epsilon 1 58.5% |
| tadalafil | `lka` | log(0.84), not estimated | Table 2 (literature value, ref 26) |
| tadalafil | `lcl` | log(1.76) L/h | Table 2 |
| tadalafil | `lvc` | log(80.6) L | Table 2 |
| tadalafil | `e_wt_cl` | 0.602 | Table 2, Effect of BW |
| tadalafil | `e_conmed_spiron_cl` | -0.400 | Table 2, Effect of SPI |
| tadalafil | `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.372^2, 0.676^2 | Table 2, IIV 37.2%, 67.6% |
| tadalafil | `propSd` | 0.333 | Table 2, epsilon 1 33.3% |
| bosentan | `lka` | log(2.47) 1/h | Table 3 |
| bosentan | `lcl` | log(8.85) L/h | Table 3 |
| bosentan | `lvc` | log(41.0) L | Table 3 |
| bosentan | `ltlag` | log(0.379) h | Table 3, absorption lag time |
| bosentan | `e_wt_cl` | 0.472 | Table 3, Effect of BW |
| bosentan | `e_alt_cl` | -0.203 | Table 3, Effect of ALT |
| bosentan | `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.329^2, 0.297^2 | Table 3, IIV 32.9%, 29.7% |
| bosentan | `propSd` | 0.590 | Table 3, epsilon 1 59.0% |
| ambrisentan | `lka` | log(1.03) 1/h | Table 3 |
| ambrisentan | `lcl` | log(0.594) L/h | Table 3 |
| ambrisentan | `lvc` | log(12.4) L | Table 3 |
| ambrisentan | `e_wt_cl` | 0.561 | Table 3, Effect of BW |
| ambrisentan | `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.608^2, 0.392^2 | Table 3, IIV 60.8%, 39.2% |
| ambrisentan | `propSd` | 0.358 | Table 3, epsilon 1 35.8% |
| all | weight centring (BWmedian) | 32.3 / 14.2 / 42.2 / 13.4 kg | Table 1 per-drug median body weight |
| bosentan | ALT centring (ALTmedian) | 16.5 IU/L | Table 1 bosentan median ALT |
| all | structure | one compartment, first-order absorption, proportional error | Methods; Results |

The CL/F equations, from the Table 2 and Table 3 footnotes, are

- sildenafil: CL/F = 60.6 x (BW/BWmedian)^0.537 x (1 + 0.633)^Bosentan
- tadalafil: CL/F = 1.76 x (BW/BWmedian)^0.602 x (1 - 0.400)^Spironolactone
- bosentan: CL/F = 8.85 x (BW/BWmedian)^0.472 x (ALT/ALTmedian)^-0.203
- ambrisentan: CL/F = 0.594 x (BW/BWmedian)^0.561

For a 0/1 indicator, (1 + 0.633)^Bosentan equals 1 + 0.633 x Bosentan, which is
how the packaged models write it. Vd/F has no covariates in any of the four
models (the authors did not search covariates on Vd/F because of its high
shrinkage).

# Clinical dosage

The paper evaluates each drug at its Japanese clinical dosage (Methods,
"Definition of clinical dosage"). The daily doses below are the paper's; the
dosing intervals are the labelled ones (sildenafil three times daily,
bosentan twice daily, tadalafil and ambrisentan once daily). The average
steady-state concentration does not depend on the interval.

```{r dosing-rules}
tau <- c(sildenafil = 8, tadalafil = 24, bosentan = 12, ambrisentan = 24)

daily_dose <- function(drug, age, wt, adult) {
  switch(drug,
    sildenafil = ifelse(adult, 60,
      ifelse(age < 1 | wt < 8, 3 * wt, ifelse(wt >= 20, 60, 30))
    ),
    tadalafil = ifelse(adult, 40, 1 * wt),
    bosentan = ifelse(adult, 250, 4 * wt),
    ambrisentan = ifelse(adult, 10, ifelse(age >= 8, 5, 0.2 * wt))
  )
}
```

# Typical-value steady-state concentration

The paper computes each patient's steady-state concentration as
Css = Dose / (CL/F), with CL/F from the patient's Bayesian estimate. With the
individual estimates unavailable, the closest deterministic check is the
typical patient at the Table 1 median age and weight of each age group, with no
interacting comedication and the median ALT (16.5 IU/L). The typical subjects
are solved to steady state with the ODE model and the average concentration
over the last dosing interval is taken with PKNCA.

```{r typical-subjects}
tbl1 <- tribble(
  ~drug, ~group, ~AGE, ~WT,
  "sildenafil", "Paediatric", 5.0, 16.5,
  "sildenafil", "Adult", 47, 48.5,
  "tadalafil", "Paediatric", 1.9, 10.7,
  "tadalafil", "Adult", 37.8, 52.3,
  "bosentan", "Paediatric", 4.8, 12,
  "bosentan", "Adult", 47, 48.5,
  "ambrisentan", "Paediatric", 1.8, 10.1,
  "ambrisentan", "Adult", 44.6, 51.4
)

# Figure 5 / Results text: median Css (ng/mL) of the Bayesian individual
# estimates in each group.
fig5 <- tribble(
  ~drug, ~group, ~cav,
  "sildenafil", "Paediatric", 25.4,
  "sildenafil", "Adult", 34.3,
  "tadalafil", "Paediatric", 461,
  "tadalafil", "Adult", 768,
  "bosentan", "Paediatric", 339,
  "bosentan", "Adult", 1221,
  "ambrisentan", "Paediatric", 164,
  "ambrisentan", "Adult", 298
)

# Steady state: 28 days of dosing for the short half-life drugs, 56 days for
# tadalafil and ambrisentan; observations over the final interval only.
run_days <- c(sildenafil = 28, tadalafil = 56, bosentan = 28, ambrisentan = 56)

build_events <- function(drug, subj, dt) {
  n_dose <- run_days[[drug]] * 24 / tau[[drug]]
  t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau[[drug]]
  obs_t <- t_last + seq(0, tau[[drug]], by = dt)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(subj)), function(i) {
    s <- subj[i, ]
    amt <- s$daily_dose * tau[[drug]] / 24
    bind_rows(
      tibble(time = (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau[[drug]], amt = amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
      tibble(time = obs_t, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
    ) |>
      mutate(id = s$id, WT = s$WT, ALT = s$ALT,
             CONMED_BOSENTAN = s$CONMED_BOSENTAN, CONMED_SPIRON = s$CONMED_SPIRON)
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(t_last = t_last)
}

typ <- tbl1 |>
  mutate(
    adult = group == "Adult",
    ALT = 16.5, CONMED_BOSENTAN = 0, CONMED_SPIRON = 0
  ) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(daily_dose = daily_dose(drug, AGE, WT, adult)) |>
  ungroup()

# One solve per typical subject: a single-subject solve of the zeroRe() model
# needs no omega and returns no `id` column.
solve_typical <- function(d, subj) {
  ev <- build_events(d, subj, dt = 0.05)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mods[[d]]), events = ev,
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6,
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  stopifnot(is.null(out$id) || all(out$id == subj$id))
  out |>
    mutate(
      drug = d, group = subj$group, id = subj$id,
      daily_dose = subj$daily_dose, tad = time - unique(ev$t_last)
    ) |>
    select(drug, group, id, tad, Cc, cl, daily_dose)
}

sim_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(drugs, function(d) {
  subj <- typ |> filter(drug == d) |> mutate(id = row_number())
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(subj)), function(i) solve_typical(d, subj[i, ])))
}))
```

```{r typical-pknca}
conc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(subj = paste(drug, group)) |>
  select(drug, group, subj, tad, Cc)
dose_typ <- sim_typ |>
  distinct(drug, group, daily_dose) |>
  mutate(subj = paste(drug, group), tad = 0, amt = daily_dose * tau[drug] / 24)
int_typ <- dose_typ |>
  transmute(drug, group, subj, start = 0, end = tau[drug], cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)

nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_typ, Cc ~ tad | drug + group + subj),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_typ, amt ~ tad | drug + group + subj),
  intervals = as.data.frame(int_typ)
))

typ_res <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "cmax", "tmax")) |>
  select(drug, group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(
    sim_typ |> distinct(drug, group, daily_dose, cl),
    by = c("drug", "group")
  ) |>
  mutate(css_closed = 1000 * daily_dose / 24 / cl) |>
  left_join(fig5 |> rename(cav_fig5 = cav), by = c("drug", "group")) |>
  mutate(pct_vs_fig5 = 100 * (cav / cav_fig5 - 1))

# The ODE steady state reproduces Css = Dose / (CL/F) for every typical
# subject (same parameters both sides: numerical error only).
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_res$cav / typ_res$css_closed - 1) < 0.005))

typ_res |>
  mutate(drug = factor(drug, drugs), group = factor(group, c("Paediatric", "Adult"))) |>
  arrange(drug, group) |>
  transmute(
    Drug = drug, Group = group,
    `Daily dose (mg)` = signif(daily_dose, 3),
    `CL/F (L/h)` = signif(cl, 3),
    `Cmax (ng/mL)` = signif(cmax, 3),
    `Cavg simulated (ng/mL)` = signif(cav, 3),
    `Dose/CL (ng/mL)` = signif(css_closed, 3),
    `Figure 5 median (ng/mL)` = cav_fig5,
    `% vs Figure 5` = round(pct_vs_fig5)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r typical-assert}
# Sildenafil, bosentan and ambrisentan: the typical patient lands within 25%
# of the published group median in both age groups. These solves are
# deterministic (no random effects), so the bound is reproducible. Tadalafil
# is discussed below and is not asserted.
chk <- typ_res |> filter(drug != "tadalafil")
stopifnot(all(abs(chk$pct_vs_fig5) < 25))
```

For sildenafil, bosentan and ambrisentan the typical patient's Css is within
25% of the published median in both age groups, and for ambrisentan within a
few percent. For tadalafil the typical patient (no spironolactone) is about 35%
(paediatric) and 45% (adult) below the published medians. Spironolactone
lowers tadalafil CL/F by 40%; with it the typical adult Css is about 720 ng/mL,
close to the published 768 ng/mL, so the gap is consistent with a high share
of spironolactone users among the patients behind Figure 5 (13 of 31 overall;
the split by age group is not reported). The paper does not print the
numerical BWmedian used for centring, and the Table 1 per-drug median is
assumed (see Assumptions).

```{r typical-profile, fig.cap = "Typical-patient steady-state profiles over one dosing interval at the clinical dosage (no interacting comedication, ALT 16.5 IU/L)."}
ggplot(sim_typ, aes(tad, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(drug, drugs), scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort and Figure 5

Figure 5 compares the Bayesian steady-state concentrations of the actual
paediatric and adult patients. The replication below draws 100 virtual
paediatric and 100 virtual adult patients per drug from the Table 1
demographics and simulates the clinical dosage to steady state with
between-subject variability.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261118)
set.seed(20261118)

# CDC 2000 50th-percentile weight-for-age, sexes averaged (cohort construction
# only, not a model parameter). Used only to order ages by weight.
cdc_age_yr <- c(c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24) / 12, 3:18)
cdc_wt_kg <- c(
  3.4, 4.4, 5.5, 6.3, 7.0, 7.9, 9.0, 9.9, 11.3, 12.5,
  14.3, 16.3, 18.3, 20.7, 23.2, 26.0, 29.2, 32.7,
  36.7, 41.3, 46.0, 50.6, 54.6, 58.0, 60.6, 62.6
)
age_for_wt <- function(wt) stats::approx(cdc_wt_kg, cdc_age_yr, xout = wt, rule = 2)$y

ranges <- tribble(
  ~drug, ~ped_age_med, ~ped_age_lo, ~ped_age_hi, ~ped_wt_med, ~ped_wt_lo, ~ped_wt_hi, ~ad_wt_med, ~ad_wt_lo, ~ad_wt_hi, ~p_bos, ~p_spi,
  "sildenafil", 5.0, 0.4, 14.8, 16.5, 6.5, 54.9, 48.5, 37.4, 58.7, 11 / 24, 0,
  "tadalafil", 1.9, 0.1, 8.3, 10.7, 5.4, 23.9, 52.3, 32.5, 73.5, 0, 13 / 31,
  "bosentan", 4.8, 2.2, 9.2, 12, 6.9, 54.9, 48.5, 38.5, 58.7, 0, 0,
  "ambrisentan", 1.8, 0.4, 8.8, 10.1, 7.1, 21.6, 51.4, 37.4, 62, 0, 0
)

n_per_group <- 100L
clamp <- function(x, lo, hi) pmin(pmax(x, lo), hi)

make_cohort <- function(r) {
  # Children with PAH are light for their age, so paediatric weight is drawn
  # around the Table 1 paediatric median directly; age follows weight along
  # the CDC curve, rescaled so the median weight maps to the median age.
  ped_wt <- clamp(r$ped_wt_med * exp(stats::rnorm(n_per_group, 0, 0.35)), r$ped_wt_lo, r$ped_wt_hi)
  ped_age <- clamp(
    r$ped_age_med * age_for_wt(ped_wt) / age_for_wt(r$ped_wt_med),
    r$ped_age_lo, r$ped_age_hi
  )
  ad_wt <- clamp(r$ad_wt_med * exp(stats::rnorm(n_per_group, 0, 0.15)), r$ad_wt_lo, r$ad_wt_hi)
  tibble(
    drug = r$drug,
    group = rep(c("Paediatric", "Adult"), each = n_per_group),
    adult = group == "Adult",
    AGE = c(ped_age, stats::runif(n_per_group, 18, 70)),
    WT = c(ped_wt, ad_wt),
    ALT = clamp(16.5 * exp(stats::rnorm(2 * n_per_group, 0, 0.4)), 7, 50),
    CONMED_BOSENTAN = stats::rbinom(2 * n_per_group, 1, r$p_bos),
    CONMED_SPIRON = stats::rbinom(2 * n_per_group, 1, r$p_spi)
  ) |>
    mutate(id = row_number(), daily_dose = daily_dose(r$drug, AGE, WT, adult))
}
cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ranges)), function(i) make_cohort(ranges[i, ])))

cohort |>
  group_by(drug = factor(drug, drugs), group) |>
  summarise(
    `Median WT (kg)` = round(median(WT), 1),
    `WT range (kg)` = paste(round(range(WT), 1), collapse = "-"),
    `Median daily dose (mg)` = signif(median(daily_dose), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r cohort-sim}
sim <- bind_rows(lapply(drugs, function(d) {
  subj <- cohort |> filter(drug == d)
  ev <- build_events(d, subj, dt = 0.25)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[d]], events = ev, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame")
  out |>
    mutate(drug = d, tad = time - unique(ev$t_last)) |>
    left_join(subj |> select(id, group, daily_dose), by = "id") |>
    select(drug, group, id, tad, Cc, cl, daily_dose)
}))
```

The steady-state concentration of each virtual patient, Css = Dose / (CL/F),
is the quantity Figure 5 plots.

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Miura 2026: steady-state concentration at the clinical dosage in paediatric and adult patients (virtual cohort, 100 per group). Whiskers span the 10th-90th percentiles as in the source figure; crosses mark the published group medians."}
css <- sim |>
  distinct(drug, group, id, cl, daily_dose) |>
  mutate(css = 1000 * daily_dose / 24 / cl)

box_stats <- css |>
  group_by(drug, group) |>
  summarise(
    ymin = quantile(css, 0.1), lower = quantile(css, 0.25), middle = median(css),
    upper = quantile(css, 0.75), ymax = quantile(css, 0.9), .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(box_stats, aes(x = factor(group, c("Paediatric", "Adult")))) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(ymin = ymin, lower = lower, middle = middle, upper = upper, ymax = ymax),
    stat = "identity", fill = "grey85"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = fig5, aes(y = cav), shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(drug, drugs), scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Css (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

The simulated steady-state profiles of the virtual cohort are analysed over
the last dosing interval with PKNCA, grouped by drug and age group. The
average concentration (`cav`) is compared with the published medians from the
Figure 5 text.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(drug, group, id, tad, Cc)
dose <- sim |>
  distinct(drug, group, id, daily_dose) |>
  mutate(tad = 0, amt = daily_dose * tau[drug] / 24)
intervals <- tibble(drug = drugs, start = 0, end = unname(tau[drugs]),
                    cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)

nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ tad | drug + group + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ tad | drug + group + id),
  intervals = as.data.frame(intervals)
))

nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "cmax", "tmax"))

nca_res |>
  group_by(drug = factor(drug, drugs), group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename(
    Drug = drug, Group = group,
    `Median Cmax (ng/mL)` = cmax, `Median Tmax (h)` = tmax, `Median Cavg (ng/mL)` = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- fig5 |>
  mutate(drug_group = paste(drug, group)) |>
  select(drug_group, cav)
simulated <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  mutate(drug_group = paste(drug, group)) |>
  select(drug_group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated, reference,
  by = "drug_group",
  units = c(cav = "ng/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp)
```

The virtual-cohort medians fall within about 30% of the published medians for
every drug and age group, with ambrisentan closest. Including the Table 1 share
of spironolactone users lifts the tadalafil medians towards the published
values compared with the typical patient without it, and including the share of
bosentan users lowers the sildenafil medians. Lower paediatric than adult
exposure at the clinical dosage is reproduced clearly for tadalafil, bosentan
and ambrisentan; the paediatric deficit is largest for bosentan (4 mg/kg/day
against a flat 250 mg/day with a weight exponent of 0.472). For sildenafil the
virtual paediatric and adult medians are similar, against a 26% deficit in the
paper that was itself not statistically significant (p = 0.064). How
bosentan use, which raises sildenafil CL/F 1.63-fold, was split between the
paper's children and adults is not reported, and the virtual cohort assigns it
equally (see Assumptions).

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Weight and ALT centring values.** The covariate equations divide by
  "BWmedian" and "ALTmedian" without printing the numbers. The per-drug Table 1
  medians are used (body weight 32.3, 14.2, 42.2 and 13.4 kg; bosentan ALT
  16.5 IU/L). Table 1 reports patient-level medians; if the authors centred on
  a dataset-level (per-concentration) median, which would be weighted towards
  the more densely sampled adults, the typical CL/F values would refer to a
  heavier patient. The close agreement for ambrisentan, whose adults and
  children are sampled in similar numbers, supports the Table 1 reading; the
  tadalafil gap (above) is the case it explains least well.
- **IIV and residual error scale.** Tables 2 and 3 give IIV and residual error
  in percent; the footnote attributing the undefined lower confidence bound to
  the square root of a negative variance shows the percentages are
  100 x sqrt(omega^2). The variances are therefore (percent / 100)^2, and the
  proportional residual SD is the percent / 100.
- **Ka.** IIV on Ka is 0 in both tables, so no eta is attached to Ka. For
  sildenafil (4.51 1/h) and tadalafil (0.84 1/h) the authors could not estimate
  Ka and took literature values; these are encoded as `fixed()`. The bosentan
  lag time has no IIV.
- **ALT unit.** Table 1 prints ALT and AST in IU/mL, which is not a plausible
  unit for values of 5-68; IU/L is assumed. ALT enters bosentan CL/F only as a
  ratio to the cohort median, so the unit does not change the model.
- **Dosing interval.** The paper gives daily doses only; the intervals used
  (sildenafil every 8 h, bosentan every 12 h, tadalafil and ambrisentan every
  24 h) follow the labels and do not affect the average concentration.
- **Virtual cohort.** Paediatric weights are drawn log-normally (SD 0.35)
  around the Table 1 paediatric median and clamped to its range; age follows
  weight along the CDC 2000 weight-for-age curve, rescaled so the median weight
  maps to the Table 1 median age, and is used only for the age-based dosing
  rules. Adult weights are drawn around the adult median (SD 0.15). Concomitant
  bosentan (sildenafil model) and spironolactone (tadalafil model) are assigned
  at the overall Table 1 frequency in both age groups because the split by age
  is not reported. ALT for the bosentan cohort is log-normal around 16.5 IU/L,
  clamped to 7-50.
- **Figure 5 comparison.** The published concentrations are Bayesian
  individual estimates for the real patients; the virtual cohort and typical
  patients can only approximate them.
- **Errata.** No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-11-18.
